note: Pass with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the battery was administered in Dutch to a Dutch community sample, but no Dutch VFQ-25 wording exists in the deposit (DataverseNL doi:10.34894/CMJXAK -- only Data_total.csv, Data_test_retest.csv and two variable-information files, whose sole VFQ entries read 'VFQ;National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire - 25 (NEI-VFQ-25)' and 'VFQ.A;... Appendix', with no per-item labels) nor in the PLOS ONE article's S1-S4 appendices (which carry the SVC only). Base fields therefore hold the instrument publisher's ENGLISH, language=Dutch, _translated columns empty: text_source=translated_substitute. (2) FORMAT: the study administered the battery online, so the SELF-administered RAND form was used rather than the interviewer-administered one; its wording differs only in the preamble and in the absence of '(READ CATEGORIES AS NEEDED)' directives. The three general preamble paragraphs are shipped as instructions; the form's six numbered administration instructions ('give it to a member of the project staff. Do not take it home') and its statement of confidentiality are NOT shipped, as they describe a paper session at a study centre that this online administration did not have. Options still read 'Circle One' on the source form; that framing is not reproduced in any shipped field. (3) resp IS NOT THE RAW RESPONSE CATEGORY. The deposit stores the RAND-converted 0-100 item scores, and data/neurodegenerative_huizinga_2019.R rescales 0/25/50/75/100 -> 0/1/2/3/4 and, for VFQ.2, 0/20/40/60/80/100 -> 0/1/2/3/4/5, so higher resp = BETTER vision-related functioning and the option order is the REVERSE of the printed 1..5/1..6 numbering for items 1-14, 15c, 16, 16a and the SAME as printed for 17-25. The printed sixth option of the difficulty items ('Stopped doing this for other reasons or not interested in doing this') is set to missing by RAND scoring and so has no row. VFQ.15, VFQ.15a and VFQ.15b are unscored skip-logic items and keep their raw 1/2 and 1/2/3 codes. (4) VFQ.15c ANOMALY: the printed 15c offers only four options (No difficulty..Extreme difficulty), yet 7 of 1,089 respondents have resp=0, one level below 'Extreme difficulty'. option_text is left blank for that row rather than guessed; the most likely reading is that the Dutch online form reused the 'stopped because of your eyesight' option from the neighbouring driving items 16/16a. (5) Interviewer read-aloud artefacts are transcribed literally rather than tidied: item 3's last option prints as 'All of the time?' and item 4's as 'Severe, or' / 'Very severe?'. (6) RIGHTS: no restriction. The questionnaire's own cover page states 'RAND hereby grants permission to use the "National Eye Institute Visual Functioning Questionnaire 25 (VFQ-25) July 1996"' and '5. No further written permission is needed for use of this NEI VFQ-25 - July 1996'; condition 4 expressly contemplates 'printing and distributing this document' subject to a credit line acknowledging that it was developed at RAND under the sponsorship of the National Eye Institute, which is an attribution requirement and not a reserved right. RAND's survey page adds 'The VFQ-25 is a public document available without charge to all researchers' and 'All of the surveys from RAND Health Care are public documents, available without charge.' No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause appears on the cover page, the FAQ or the RAND page. (7) Step 3b: the live data is 29 items VFQ.1-VFQ.25 plus the irregular VFQ.15a/15b/15c/16a driving sub-items, exactly the VFQ-25's own numbering, and matches no sibling instrument in this battery; the 13 optional appendix items VFQ.A1-A13 the study also administered are excluded by the processing script and are not in this table. ORCHESTRATOR STEP 5b RE-CHECK (2026-09-09): caveats (3) and (4) are CONFIRMED against primary sources, not taken on report. (3) The rescale is verified by reading data/neurodegenerative_huizinga_2019.R directly: it recodes VFQ.2 0/20/40/60/80/100 -> 0..5 and every other VFQ item 0/25/50/75/100 -> 0..4, with a TRUE ~ resp fall-through that leaves the unscored skip items VFQ.15/15a/15b on their raw codes -- exactly as described. The deposit's raw frequencies match the quoted evidence (VFQ.1 32/287/589/368/96; VFQ.2 1/22/248/833/268; VFQ.15b 7/80/8) and VFQ.24 has 1270/1344 = 94.5% at 100, anchoring direction. (4) The VFQ.15c anomaly is confirmed exactly: in Data_total.csv VFQ.15c has n=1089 with raw values 0:7, 25:1, 50:2, 75:32, 100:1047, so 7 respondents do sit one level below the printed four-option floor; option_text for that row is correctly left null rather than guessed. ONE LABEL CORRECTION to caveat (5): the trailing-question-mark options ('All of the time?', 'Severe, or', 'Very severe?') are described there as interviewer read-aloud artefacts, which could be misread as meaning the interviewer form was shipped. It was not -- the shipped instructions are the SELF-administered wording ('The following is a survey with statements...'), not the interviewer form's ('I'm going to read you some statements...'). The trailing punctuation is a legacy artefact carried inside the self-administered form itself, and transcribing it literally rather than tidying it is correct. RIGHTS independently verified from the questionnaire PDF text: conditions 1-5 confirmed verbatim, condition 4 is an attribution requirement ('will provide a credit line when printing and distributing this document') and condition 5 reads 'No further written permission is needed'; no fee, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term appears. Verdict ship is correct.

Pass with caveats. (1) No response-option wording exists anywhere in the record: the S2 File questionnaire (pone.0323879.s002.docx) prints the 20 statements with no scale, no anchors and no instruction line, and the paper's Measures section (3.2) names only 'a four-item scale derived from Al-Swidi and Saleh' without stating the 1-5 coding direction. option_text is therefore blank for all five resp levels and instructions is blank -- deliberately not padded with the scale numbers. (2) Administration language is not stated. The survey ran on Google Forms to Vietnamese Generation Z, but the paper never mentions a translation or back-translation, the only questionnaire deposited is in English, and the S1 data file carries an unexplained 'E_L' (English level) covariate; language is left empty rather than asserting either a Vietnamese or an English administration. If a Vietnamese form is ever located this table becomes a translated_substitute backfill candidate. (3) Two item strings carried a trailing space in the .docx and were stripped; no other change to the wording. (4) The four attitude statements are unnumbered in S2, so their tie to G_ATT_1..4 is presentation order -- see the verification row, which is PARTIAL for exactly that reason.

Item wording transcribed verbatim from S2 File 'Research instruments' (10.1371/journal.pone.0323879.s002), whose 'Green perceived behavioral control' block lists exactly four sentences in order but carries no item codes; codes G_PBC_1..4 are the S1 File's own column headers and the processing script (data/ngo_2025_green_purchasing.py) melts them by name, so the code<->column tie is exact while the code<->sentence tie is an order inference (mapping_basis=paper_order, verification NO_ROUTE). item 4 is shipped without a terminal period because the source has none. option_text is blank for all 20 rows: neither the article nor S2 states the 1-5 anchors anywhere, and padding an unlabelled scale point with its own number is barred. Administration language is not stated: the sample is Vietnamese Gen Z recruited via Vietnamese-language Facebook hashtags, but the only instrument document deposited is English and the deposit carries an 'E_L' (English level) covariate; if the Google Form was administered in Vietnamese, the shipped wording is the study's own English version rather than what respondents read. Rights: items are ad-hoc TPB perceived-behavioural-control statements adapted from Chaudhary & Bisai, reproduced in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS supplement; no reserved-rights clause locatable for the instrument, so silence-is-permission applies. RESPONSE-DATA ANOMALY (not an item-text issue, flagged for the corpus-trust pass): in all five constructs of this deposit the odd-numbered items average ~2.7 and the even-numbered ~3.7 - G_ATT 2.72/3.71/2.68/3.73, G_SN 2.73/3.74/2.68/3.70, G_PBC 2.61/3.61/2.64/3.62, G_PI 2.67/3.62/2.70/3.71, G_PB 2.70/3.76/2.76/3.68 - an alternating regularity across 20 items of five distinct constructs that no item content explains and that the paper never mentions. ORCHESTRATOR STEP 5b RE-CHECK (2026-09-09): the alternating anomaly is CONFIRMED and sharpened. All 20 means recomputed independently from the S1 File deposit reproduce the agent's figures to 3 d.p. (G_ATT 2.717/3.713/2.679/3.730; G_SN 2.730/3.738/2.679/3.696; G_PBC 2.612/3.608/2.637/3.624; G_PI 2.667/3.624/2.696/3.709; G_PB 2.705/3.759/2.755/3.684) -- every odd-numbered item falls in 2.61-2.76 and every even-numbered one in 3.61-3.76, with no overlap, across all five constructs. REFINEMENT the agent did not establish: this is a pure LOCATION shift, not two separate blocks. Pooled over all 20 items the odd-item response distribution is 1:148 2:831 3:1019 4:357 5:15 and the even-item distribution is 1:6 2:132 3:821 4:1046 5:365 -- the same shape displaced by about one scale point. The correlation structure does NOT split by parity: odd-odd r (n=45) median .236, even-even (n=45) median .213, odd-even (n=100) median .257, and within every construct r(item1,item2) (.589-.643) is the same size as r(item1,item3) (.623-.651). So the parity split is a systematic ~1-point offset on alternating columns, not a content or method factor. This is a property of the deposit's response data, not an itemtext defect; public_note deliberately left empty and it is referred to the corpus-trust line rather than the public issues page.

Clean pass with three caveats. (1) The paper's Measures section says green purchasing (G_PB) 'was assessed using a three-item measure from Joshi and Rahman', but the study's own S2 File (Research instruments) lists FOUR sentences under 'Green purchasing behavior', the S1 File data has four columns G_PB_1..G_PB_4, and paper Table 2 reports four loadings for the G_PB construct; the 'three-item' phrase is an error in the prose and four items were extracted. (2) No response anchors are published anywhere -- neither the article (no '5-point'/'Likert'/anchor wording appears in the full text) nor S2, which prints the item sentences with no scale legend -- so option_text is blank for all 20 rows rather than padded; resp 1-5 is carried from the live data. (3) The study surveyed Vietnamese Generation Z and the paper never states the language of administration or any translation procedure; the only instrument published in the deposit or supplements is the English S2 File, which is what was shipped, so 'language' and the _translated columns are omitted. If the survey was in fact fielded in Vietnamese, this table's item_text is an English rendering the study itself published, and the administered wording is not recoverable from the deposit.
